alternatives.root_cause: Currency was cut off from the network, so callers hung identically while currency itself kept running.
alternatives.why_not: A partitioned service normally still writes its own log complaining it cannot reach dependencies; currency wrote nothing at all and also published no metrics, which fits a stopped process better - though the absent log stream leaves this not fully excluded.

alternatives.root_cause: Checkout itself hung internally after fetching cart and catalog data.
alternatives.why_not: Checkout demonstrably executed outbound calls to cart and product-catalog during the incident window and its error ratio stayed flat, so its process was alive; the stall begins precisely at the hop where currency should answer.

alternatives.root_cause: A flag flip in flagd enabled a failing code path in the checkout flow.
alternatives.why_not: flagd resolutions complete in well under a millisecond in healthy traces and the stall is not located at a flag evaluation; the symptom is an unanswered currency hop and a deadline, not a failing flagged branch.

verdict.summary: The currency service stopped serving while its socket still accepted connections, so checkout's Convert call during order preparation hung until the 15s frontend deadline, failing every checkout-path dependency downstream of it.
verdict.reasoning: Post-onset checkout traces (tr_fc5759dc8a7f) show the request reaching checkout, which successfully completes cart GetCart and product-catalog GetProduct calls, after which the trace stops: the checkout PlaceOrder parent span never closes, frontend/POST burns ~15000ms of pure self-time and the ingress errors on deadline. In the healthy pre-onset traces (tr_efd554291d08) the very next hop after GetCart/GetProduct inside prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart is currency/Currency/Convert; no currency span appears anywhere after 07:59, and currency produced no log lines (tr_d6d1b11dbafd) and no metric samples at all in the incident window (tr_e2d4503890f1). Callers hanging to their deadlines while the dependency emits nothing - no logs, no spans, no metrics - is the signature of a frozen process rather than one returning errors; checkout's own error ratio never rises (tr_297317623069) and payment logged normal completed transactions up to the onset (tr_c4954e441b1d), consistent with the leaf services being starved of work rather than broken themselves. No change was recorded for currency or checkout (tr_3396f4a5893b, tr_c26154292e9d), ruling out a deploy or config edit as the mechanism.
open_questions: Currency emitted no log lines even in the pre-onset baseline window, so silence alone does not fully discriminate a freeze from a network partition - a partitioned currency would be expected to log reachability complaints, but this log stream may never have carried currency output.
Whether currency's socket genuinely still accepts (freeze) or connections are being blackholed at the network layer was not directly observed.
Why accounting and fraud-detection alert was not confirmed; most likely absence of order events rather than their own failure.
